notes: Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2, and USMC Operations vol. I, Part VI, ch. 4, agree that on 22 August 1942 the first AAF planes, five P-400s of the 67th Fighter Squadron led by Captain Dale D. Brannon, landed on Guadalcanal after flying up from New Caledonia via Espiritu Santo. Confidence 0.7.

current_activity: nine more P-400s arriving at Henderson Field
notes: Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2, and USMC Operations vol. I, Part VI, ch. 4, agree that on 27 August 1942 nine more P-400s of the 67th Fighter Squadron arrived (Craven: flown in by Captain John A. Thompson). Craven says the squadron was then under operational control of Marine Aircraft Wing One; the 1st MAW headquarters detachment itself arrived on 3 September (USMC Operations, ch. 5 and Appendix C). On this date the on-island air command was MAG-23. Confidence 0.7 for the arrival; the wing-OPCON wording is recorded in the relation notes.
